Mean correlation by year: 2008: 0.49, 2009: 0.52, 2010: 0.53, 2011: 0.50, 2012: 0.45, 2013: 0.46, 2014: 0.33, 2015: 0.42, 2016: 0.41, 2017: 0.27, 2018: 0.41, 2019: 0.37, 2020: 0.56, 2021: 0.39, 2022: 0.51, 2023: 0.41.

The protocol's planning range was ρ̄ = 0.3–0.7 (§V2.1). Measured: ρ̄ = 0.48, so the 26 tickers carry the information of about **2 independent assets**, and fewer in stress (1.8), exactly when a de-risking agent should act. ^GDAXI closes 4.5 h before the US ETFs, so its same-day correlations are understated; excluding it changes ρ̄ by +0.001.

## 3. Minimum backtest length: the best Sharpe that luck alone produces

Best annual Sharpe ratio expected from N zero-skill configurations: the expected maximum (Bailey & López de Prado 2014, V[SR] = 1/T) and, in brackets, the upper bound √(2 ln N / T) (Bailey et al. 2014), which the protocol's table in §V2.2 uses.

| N trials | T = development (16.24 y) | T = validation blocks (9.70 y) | From the trial log (correlated trials) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 (now) | 0.45 (≤ 0.58) | 0.58 (≤ 0.76) | 0.17 |
| 26 (v2 cap) | 0.50 (≤ 0.63) | 0.65 (≤ 0.82) | 0.19 |
| 50 (Part I budget) | 0.56 (≤ 0.69) | 0.73 (≤ 0.90) | 0.22 |

- Trials are compared on the concatenated validation blocks (9.70 years), not on the whole development period, so **the validation column is the relevant one**: luck alone can be expected to produce a best Sharpe near 0.58 from the 16 trials so far.
- The trial log's cross-trial variance of daily Sharpe ratios is 3.68e-05, about 11× smaller than independent zero-skill trials would show (4.09e-04). Our trials are strongly correlated (mostly long the same ETFs). The deflated Sharpe ratio uses this variance (Part I §10a.3), so its hurdle SR₀ (last column) is much lower than the independent-trial bound.

Minimum backtest length (MinBTL): years of validation data needed before the best of N zero-skill trials is *expected* to stay below a given annual Sharpe; in brackets the protocol's bound 2 ln N / SR².

| N trials | SR 0.25 | SR 0.5 | SR 1.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 (now) | 52 (89) | 13 (22) | 3.2 (5.5) |
| 26 (v2 cap) | 65 (104) | 16 (26) | 4.1 (6.5) |
| 50 (Part I budget) | 83 (125) | 21 (31) | 5.2 (7.8) |

## Q1. Close-time leak in ^GDAXI's residual features: **found and fixed**

The day-t residual of ^GDAXI subtracts factor returns built from the US ETFs' day-t returns, which settle 4.5 h after the DAX close. The US afternoon move then shows up in the DAX's *next-day* return, so the v1 residual 'predicts' it. Medians over the 5 folds for the validation rows:

| Quantity | v1 pipeline (as in M4) | v2 pipeline (lagged one bar) |
|---|---|---|
| corr(residₜ, next-day return), development, n = 4123 (SE ≈ 0.016) | -0.147 | +0.027 |
| corr(resid_cum30ₜ, next-day return), development, n = 4123 (SE ≈ 0.016) | -0.028 | +0.003 |
| timing IC of resid (LC3 definition), validation blocks | -0.148 | -0.006 |
| rule 'long tomorrow iff residₜ < 0': gross Sharpe | 1.48 | 0.15 |
| same rule, net Sharpe at 10 bp + 1 bp | 0.26 | -0.89 |
| same rule, switches per 100 bars | 56 | 56 |
| selective rule 'flat tomorrow iff z(resid)ₜ > 2', net Sharpe (best of 5 thresholds, biased up) | 0.47 | 0.00 |
| selective rule, switches per 100 bars | 6 | 6 |
| buy-and-hold net Sharpe, same blocks | 0.39 | 0.39 |

Fix: `rl/features_m4.py`, `pipeline: v2`: the cross-asset (residual) features of early-close tickers use the t−1 value; context features (VIX) already used t−1 for every ticker. Test `test_q1_early_close_ticker_never_sees_same_day_us_returns`. All v2 configurations, R0′ included, use pipeline v2. ^GDAXI is the only early-close ticker among the 33 (§V2.3).

Reading: the leak is large in gross terms, but trading it daily costs more than it earns. Even the generous selective rule beats buy-and-hold net of costs by only +0.08. Whether the M4 agents used it at all is answered by their timing IC in Step 0a.

## Q3. Daily moves beyond 8σ (σ = ex-ante EWMA-60 volatility of the previous day)

12 moves in the development period. *Market-wide* = at least 3 of the 33 tickers moved beyond 4σ that day. A single-ticker move counts as *genuine* if the close lies within the day's high–low range and the next day does not reverse more than 75 % of it (a bad print usually fails one of the two).

| Ticker | Date | Return | z | Next day | Tickers beyond 4σ | Class | Event (general knowledge) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LQD | 2008-09-16 | -6.3% | -15.1 | -4.6% | 1 | single-ticker, genuine | Lehman week (bankruptcy filed 2008-09-15) |
| GLD | 2013-04-15 | -8.8% | -8.0 | +1.1% | 12 | market-wide | gold crash |
| SLV | 2013-04-15 | -12.6% | -8.9 | +2.6% | 12 | market-wide | gold crash |
| EWU | 2016-06-24 | -12.0% | -8.6 | -4.0% | 18 | market-wide | UK Brexit referendum result |

| EWZ | 2017-05-18 | -16.3% | -9.9 | +6.7% | 1 | single-ticker, genuine | Brazil: Temer/JBS recordings scandal |
| ^VIX | 2018-02-05 | +115.6% | +9.7 | -19.7% | 18 | market-wide | volatility spike ('Volmageddon') |
| XLE | 2020-03-09 | -20.1% | -9.9 | +4.7% | 22 | market-wide | COVID-19 sell-off and OPEC+ oil price war |
| EWA | 2020-03-09 | -11.8% | -8.8 | +8.6% | 22 | market-wide | COVID-19 sell-off and OPEC+ oil price war |
| EWC | 2020-03-09 | -12.4% | -11.3 | +2.5% | 22 | market-wide | COVID-19 sell-off and OPEC+ oil price war |
| USO | 2020-03-09 | -25.3% | -11.2 | +11.0% | 22 | market-wide | COVID-19 sell-off and OPEC+ oil price war |
| FXI | 2022-03-16 | +21.2% | +8.9 | -3.7% | 2 | single-ticker, genuine | China: State Council pledge to support markets |

Result: **0 possible bad prints**; every flagged move is a real market event, and all of them agree with the fresh download (Q2). The event labels are from general knowledge and were not checked against a source here.
Known structural change that the 8σ scan cannot see: USO changed from front-month to longer-dated oil futures and did a 1-for-8 reverse split in April–May 2020 (general knowledge, not verified here). The adjusted prices absorb the split, and the series is what an investor in USO actually earned, so **no window is masked**.

## Q4. Zero or constant volume

1 of 33 tradable tickers have zero-volume or 20-day-constant-volume bars in development. ^VIX volume is zero on 100% of days; ^VIX is a context feature (level only), so its volume is never read.

| Ticker | Zero-volume bars | Bars with constant 20-day volume |
|---|---|---|
| ^GDAXI | 9 | 0 |

Fix: `pipeline: v2` masks `vol_rel20` on those bars (set to the neutral 0 after z-scoring). Test `test_q4_zero_or_constant_volume_is_masked`.

## Q5. Dates, duplicates, stale prices and forward filling

- Duplicate dates: 0; non-monotonic series: 0; bars with a missing open/high/low/close: 0.
- Bars per year: 251.9 – 253.9 (exchange calendars; ^GDAXI follows Xetra).
- Days with an unchanged close: 1289 of 135036 ticker-days; longest run 2 day(s); unchanged **and** zero volume (a typical stale bar): 0.
- No tradable bar is forward-filled (Part I §3). Each ticker is backtested on its own bars (`harness/backtest.py`). In the equal-weight portfolio a ticker without a bar that day (e.g. a German holiday for ^GDAXI) contributes 0 % (`harness/backtest.portfolio`). Forward filling exists only inside the residual-factor panel, where a missing day is a 0 % return (`rl/features_m4.residual_returns`).

## Consequences

- **Q1, Q4 (fixed in `pipeline: v2`)** change agent features only. Every v2 configuration uses pipeline v2, and the reference is re-run as R0′ (Step 0d). The baselines read prices only, so they cannot change; they were re-scored in Step 0a anyway (`experiments/reports/V2_0a_rescore.md`).
- **Q2, Q3, Q5:** the price data is correct as frozen. No re-download, no masking.
- **Sections 1–3:** about 2 independent assets, 5–6 drawdown events and a luck level near Sharpe 0.58 for the best of 16 trials. This is why v2 tries few configurations and uses structure (anchor, cost-aware head) instead of more search.
